0.long_answer: The FDA-approved medication for pituitary-driven Cushing’s disease in adults who are not candidates for pituitary surgery or who have persistent disease following surgery is osilodrostat, sold under the brand name Isturisa. This drug works as an inhibitor of the enzyme 11β-hydroxylase (CYP11B1), which plays a crucial role in cortisol synthesis. By inhibiting this enzyme, osilodrostat reduces cortisol production, helping to manage the high cortisol levels characteristic of Cushing’s disease. Its approval was based on clinical studies that demonstrated its effectiveness in normalizing cortisol levels in patients who had either failed surgery or could not undergo the procedure.
